text: #805, built by hand since the factory's own runs would wait in the queue it fixes: processes sharing Codex's sign-in take its turn lock in the order they asked. A process's next run took the lock the instant its last run freed it, while another process tried once a second, so a busy watcher's queue kept the other waiting: ask3d#33's review waited over two hours behind Invariant's drafts and builds. Each process waiting for the lock now holds a ticket in Codex's home, named for when it asked and locked while it waits, made under a temporary name and renamed into place once locked. A process takes the lock only when no live ticket is older than its own, and a ticket nobody holds is a dead process's, which the next waiter removes. Waiting stays cancellable and still checks that its work is wanted (#677); a process without a ticket, an older binary's, is still kept apart by the lock itself.
